page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.12xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory footprint totals 96.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with support for VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but provides no local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring attached cloud disks for persistence.

Benchmark results place the instance in the top 25 percent across multiple compute and memory metrics. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2008.0 and a multi-core score of 18295.0, matched by a PassMark CPU score of 62853.8 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 73776.27. Vectorized operations and multi-threaded decompression perform strongly, reaching 257.2 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 64.43 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. However, uncached memory bandwidth registers in the middle 50 percent at 113.72 GB/sec for large block reads and 83.95 GB/sec for writes, with static web serving throughput also sitting at an average 40.48 GB/sec.

From an efficiency perspective, the 1:2 memory configuration maximizes processor density for CPU-bound tasks, avoiding expenditure on unneeded memory capacity. The primary hardware tradeoff is the total absence of bundled local NVMe storage, meaning disk I/O performance relies entirely on external network block storage. Given its strong compilation (46733.0 in Geekbench Clang) and execution capabilities, the instance fits software build pipelines, distributed CI/CD runners, batch processing, ray tracing, and compute-focused database or in-memory caching nodes.
